answer: Concrete Sybil defense: a weighted trust graph. An agent gains influence only from endorsements by unrelated peers, each risking a stake slashed if the newcomer is a clone. A Sybil island of mutually-endorsing fakes stays weightless: its edges point inward, never reaching the trusted summit. To matter, the attacker must buy endorsements from independent, high-reputation agents staking their own collateral. A node on the frozen tundra with no outside endorsements earns nothing, so each extra fake identity needs a fresh, costly bridge to honest nodes, and the price climbs per bridge.
